subject: maths
title: Counting in 2s, 5s and 10s
seo_title: Year 1 Counting in 2s, 5s and 10s Worksheets: Equal Groups and Sharing
standard_text: Count in multiples of twos, fives and tens; solve one-step problems involving multiplication and division, by calculating the answer using concrete objects, pictorial representations and arrays with the support of the teacher.
meta_desc: Free Year 1 maths worksheets on counting in 2s, 5s and 10s: socks, hands, coins and tens sticks, equal groups, arrays and sharing equally. 100 picture questions with an answer key, following the National Curriculum.
key_sub: 3 pairs of socks: 2, 4, 6, so 6 socks. Equal groups all have the same number. To share fairly, give 1 to each until none are left.
body_html:
Counting in 2s, 5s and 10s

Some things come in groups. Socks come in 2s. A hand has 5 fingers. A ten frame holds 10. Count the groups by saying every 2nd, 5th or 10th number. It is faster than counting in 1s.

Count inSayThink of
2s2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12pairs of socks, eyes, 2p coins
5s5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30fingers on a hand, 5p coins
10s10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60two hands, 10p coins, tens sticks

Equal groups and arrays

Equal groups all have the same number. Say “3 groups of 5” or “3 lots of 5”. Count in 5s to find how many altogether. An array is equal rows. Count a row at a time.

Example

How many socks are in 5 pairs?

Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.

Answer: 10 socks

Sharing equally

To share, give 1 to each, then 1 more to each, until none are left. Sharing is fair when everyone gets the same.

Example

Share 12 biscuits equally between 3 children.

Give them out one at a time. Each child gets 4. Check: 4, 8, 12.

Answer: 4 biscuits each

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Going back to 1s at the end: 2, 4, 6, 7Keep the same jump: 2, 4, 6, 8
Missing a group: 4 hands, but only 5, 10, 15Touch each group as you count: 5, 10, 15, 20
Counting the groups, not the things: 3 pairs = 3 socksEach pair is 2: 2, 4, 6 socks
Sharing unfairly: 10 sweets as 6 and 4Give 1 at a time to each plate: 5 and 5

faq.q: When do children learn to count in 2s, 5s and 10s?
faq.a: In Year 1. The National Curriculum says pupils should count in multiples of twos, fives and tens, and use objects, pictures and arrays to solve simple grouping and sharing problems.

faq.q: Do Year 1 children learn times tables?
faq.a: Not formally. In Year 1 they count in 2s, 5s and 10s and talk about “groups of”. The 2, 5 and 10 times tables, with the × sign, come in Year 2.

faq.q: How can I help my child count in 2s, 5s and 10s at home?
faq.a: Count real things: pairs of socks in 2s, fingers in 5s and 10p coins in 10s. Ask your child to touch each group as they say the number.

faq.q: How do you teach sharing equally in Year 1?
faq.a: Use plates and small objects. Give one to each plate in turn until none are left, then check that every plate has the same number.
